subject: Chemistry
title: Werner’s Theory, Complex vs. Double Salt Taxonomy, & Ligand Classification
topics: Werner's Dual Valency Theory (1893): Primary Valency (Ionizable, Non-directional, Oxidation State) vs Secondary Valency (Non-ionizable, Directional, Coordination Number)
Double Salts (Mohr's Salt, Carnallite, Potash Alum) vs Coordination Complexes (K₄[Fe(CN)₆], [Cu(NH₃)₄]SO₄)
1.1 Ligand Denticity Classes (Monodentate, Bidentate: en, ox²⁻, gly⁻, dmg⁻; Polydentate: EDTA⁴⁻)
Ambidentate Ligand Binding Modes (Nitrito -NO₂⁻/-ONO⁻, Thiocyanato -SCN⁻/-NCS⁻, Cyanido -CN⁻/-NC⁻)
The Chelate Effect (Thermodynamic Stability & Entropy Increase ΔS° > 0)
quickSummary: Werner's Dual Valency: Primary valency is ionizable/non-directional (Oxidation State); Secondary valency is non-ionizable/directional (Coordination Number). Double salts dissociate completely into simple ions; coordination complexes retain complex ion integrity. Ligand denticity ranges from monodentate to hexadentate (EDTA⁴⁻). Ambidentate ligands bind via either of two donor atoms.
summary: Master Werner's dual valency theory, double salt vs coordination complex differences, ligand denticity classes, and the chelate effect.

summaryBox.title: Werner's Dual Valency (1893)
summaryBox.takeaway: Primary Valency = Ionizable, Non-directional, Oxidation State. Secondary Valency = Non-ionizable, Directional, Coordination Number & 3D Geometry.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
WERNER'S DUAL VALENCY THEORY (1893)
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                           ▼
  PRIMARY VALENCY                                            SECONDARY VALENCY
  ├── Ionizable; satisfies negative charges                  ├── Non-ionizable; satisfied by neutral/anionic ligands
  ├── Non-directional; corresponds to **Oxidation State**    ├── Directional; corresponds to **Coordination Number**
  └── Depicted as dashed lines in structures                 └── Defines fixed 3D spatial geometry (Octahedral/Square)

                     DOUBLE SALTS vs COORDINATION COMPLEXES
                     
   DOUBLE SALTS (*e.g., Mohr's Salt, Carnallite, Potash Alum*):
   ├── Completely dissociate into individual constituent simple ions when dissolved in water.
   └── Lose their structural identity in aqueous solution (*e.g., $\text{FeSO}_4\cdot(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4\cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{2+} + 2\text{NH}_4^+ + 2\text{SO}_4^{2-}$*).
   
   COORDINATION COMPLEXES (*e.g., $\text{K}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6], [\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]\text{SO}_4$*):
   ├── Do NOT dissociate into simple constituent ions in water; retain complex ion identity.
   └── Complex ion remains intact in aqueous solution (*e.g., $\text{K}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6] \rightarrow 4\text{K}^+ + [\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$*).
conceptBreakdown.content: Coordination chemistry evaluates metal-ligand complexes where a central metal ion acts as a Lewis acid (electron-pair acceptor) bound to surrounding neutral or anionic Ligands acting as Lewis bases (electron-pair donors) via coordinate covalent bonds.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Denticity is the number of donor atoms through which a ligand binds directly to a single central metal ion.
- **Chelate Effect**: When a multidentate ligand binds a central metal ion to form a closed 5- or 6-membered ring structure (Chelate Ring), the thermodynamic stability of the complex increases dramatically ($\Delta S^\circ > 0$ due to increased total particle count upon ligand substitution).

quickRevision: Secondary valency = Coordination Number (non-ionizable, directional, defines geometry).
Double salts dissociate completely into simple ions; complexes retain complex ion integrity.
EDTA⁴⁻ is a hexadentate ligand (2 N + 4 O donors).
Ambidentate ligands (-NO₂⁻, -SCN⁻, -CN⁻) coordinate through either donor atom.
Chelate rings (5/6-membered) enhance stability through entropy gain (ΔS° > 0).
